name: Carrier, SIM and cell tower
plain: Sites cannot read your mobile carrier, SIM or tower ID.
meaning: Only the Network Information type (cellular) on Android Chromium and the server-side IP to ASN lookup reveal the carrier (about 100 major carriers). No MCC, MNC, SIM or tower API exists on the web.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: IP to ASN lookup (server side)

limits.headline: Can't see your mobile carrier, SIM, or cell tower from a web page
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: Check if you are on cellular or Wi-Fi in Chrome on Android
Look up your carrier from your IP address on the server
cannot: See your carrier code or tower ID
Get a carrier name directly; only a server lookup by IP gives a guess

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot read your mobile carrier, SIM or cell tower.
story.for_you: A page cannot tell which phone company you use from your phone. It can guess from your internet address, and Android Chrome may report a rough connection type like 4G or Wi-Fi.
story.for_makers: Marketers and fraud teams want the carrier to target offers, verify identity and spot fraud. The web does not give it. They use IP address lookups that name the network provider instead.

use_cases.example: A mobile ad network wants your carrier and uses the network of your IP address to guess.
A bank wanted to match your SIM to your account for fraud and uses a separate phone number check.
A streaming site wanted to know if you are on cellular data to lower quality and uses the connection type hint.
A cloud gaming site wanted tower quality for stream tuning and measures speed in the page instead.
A fraud team wanted to flag SIM swap risk and relies on server side checks.
A roaming offer site wanted to know when you travel and uses your IP country.
A telco partner wanted to match visits to subscribers and needs an agreement and sign-in.

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
